title: Alternating permutations, Euler numbers, and the cd-index of $\mathfrak{S}_n$
key_idea: Alternating permutations (where $w_1 < w_2 > w_3 < w_4 > \cdots$) are counted by Euler numbers $E_n$, with OGF $\sec x + \tan x$. The cd-index $\Phi_n$ encodes all descent-set statistics $\beta(S)$ in a polynomial in two non-commuting variables $c$ and $d$, with only $E_n$ monomials instead of $2^{n-1}$ in the ab-index.
summary: Section 1.6 proves that the EGF of Euler numbers is $\sec x + \tan x$ (Prop 1.6.1). It introduces min-max trees and the M-equivalence on permutations, showing that each equivalence class contains exactly one alternating permutation. The cd-index $\Phi_n$ — an element of $\mathbb{Z}\langle c,d\rangle$ with $c=a+b$, $d=ab+ba$ — packages descent-set information compactly.

notation.description: EGF of Euler numbers $E_0, E_1, E_2, \ldots$

definitions.statement: A permutation $w = w_1\cdots w_n$ is **alternating** if $w_1 < w_2 > w_3 < w_4 > \cdots$, i.e., $D(w) = \{2, 4, 6, \ldots\} \cap [n-1]$. It is **reverse alternating** if $w_1 > w_2 < w_3 > \cdots$. The **Euler number** $E_n = \#$(alternating permutations in $\mathfrak{S}_n$).

For a permutation $w \in \mathfrak{S}_n$, the **characteristic monomial** $u_{D(w)} = e_1 e_2 \cdots e_{n-1}$ where $e_i = a$ if $i \notin D(w)$ and $e_i = b$ if $i \in D(w)$. The **ab-index** of $\mathfrak{S}_n$ is $\Psi_n = \sum_{w \in \mathfrak{S}_n} u_{D(w)}$.

Setting $c = a+b$ and $d = ab+ba$, one can rewrite $\Psi_n = \Phi_n(c,d)$ as a polynomial in $c$ and $d$ (the **cd-index**). This is the Theorem 1.6.3 assertion.

propositions.title: EGF of Euler numbers
propositions.proof_sketch: Consider splitting alternating permutations of $[n+1]$ at their maximum. If $n+1$ appears at position $k+1$, then the first $k$ elements form an alternating permutation of a $k$-element subset, and the last $n-k$ elements form a reverse alternating permutation. The symmetry $E_n = E_n'$ (reverse alternating = same count) gives a recurrence $2E_{n+1} = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}E_k E_{n-k}$, which translates to the ODE $2y' = y^2+1$ with $y(0)=1$, whose solution is $\sec x + \tan x$.

propositions.title: Flip equivalence and Euler numbers
propositions.statement: The number of flip-equivalence classes of increasing $(1,2)$-trees on $[n]$ equals $E_n$.
propositions.proof_sketch: The flip operation on trees corresponds to the M-equivalence on permutations (introduced via min-max trees). Each equivalence class has size $2^{\iota(w)}$ and contains exactly one alternating permutation. The ODE argument gives $E_n$ classes.

propositions.title: cd-index monotonicity
propositions.statement: Let $S, T \subseteq [n-1]$. If $\omega(S) \subset \omega(T)$ (strict containment), then $\beta_n(S) < \beta_n(T)$, where $\omega(S) = \{i \in [n-2] : \text{exactly one of } i, i+1 \in S\}$.

theorems.title: cd-index theorem
theorems.statement: The ab-index $\Psi_n = \sum_{w\in\mathfrak{S}_n} u_{D(w)}$ can be written as a polynomial $\Phi_n$ in $c = a+b$ and $d = ab+ba$: $\Psi_n = \Phi_n(c,d)$. This polynomial has **nonnegative integer coefficients** and has exactly $F_n$ (Fibonacci number) distinct monomials, compared to $2^{n-1}$ for the ab-index.
theorems.proof_sketch: The M-equivalence classes (of size $2^{\iota(w)}$) each contain exactly one alternating permutation, and each generates a single $cd$-monomial. The positivity follows from this combinatorial interpretation.

corollaries.title: Maximum beta value
corollaries.statement: $\beta_n(S) \leq E_n$ for all $S \subseteq [n-1]$, with equality iff $S = \{1,3,5,\ldots\} \cap [n-1]$ or $S = \{2,4,6,\ldots\} \cap [n-1]$ (the alternating and reverse-alternating sets).
corollaries.proof_sketch: Follows from Proposition 1.6.4 and the characterization of maximal $\omega$ sets.

exercises.statement: Show that $E_{2n} = (-1)^n$ (sec coefficient) and these are related to the Bernoulli numbers.
hints: The Taylor series of sec x gives the secant (or tangent) numbers.

text_passages.label: Definition — Alternating permutation
text_passages.preview: $w$ is alternating if $w_1 < w_2 > w_3 < w_4 > \cdots$ (descents at even positions). Euler number $E_n$ = count in $\mathfrak{S}_n$. $E_0=1,E_1=1,E_2=1,E_3=2,E_4=5,E_5=16,\ldots$

text_passages.label: Proposition 1.6.1 — EGF of Euler numbers
text_passages.preview: $\sum_{n\geq 0}E_n x^n/n! = \sec x + \tan x$. Derived from splitting at the maximum: recurrence $2E_{n+1}=\sum_k\binom{n}{k}E_kE_{n-k}$ and ODE $2y'=y^2+1$.

text_passages.text: The **min-max tree** $M(w)$ of a permutation $w$ is built recursively: the minimum (or maximum, alternating) is the root, and subtrees continue left and right. The **M-equivalence** $v \sim^M w$ if $v$ is obtained from $w$ by a sequence of $\psi_i$ operators that flip descent/ascent at position $i$. Each equivalence class has size $2^{\iota(w)}$ and contains exactly one alternating permutation.

text_passages.label: Definition — cd-index
text_passages.preview: ab-index $\Psi_n = \sum_w u_{D(w)}$ where $u_S = e_1\cdots e_{n-1}$, $e_i=a$ if $i\notin S$, $e_i=b$ if $i\in S$. Setting $c=a+b$, $d=ab+ba$ gives $\Psi_n = \Phi_n(c,d)$ — the cd-index.

text_passages.label: Theorem 1.6.3 — cd-index theorem
text_passages.preview: $\Psi_n = \Phi_n(c,d)$ for $c=a+b$, $d=ab+ba$. The cd-index has nonneg integer coefficients and $F_n$ monomials (Fibonacci) vs $2^{n-1}$ for the ab-index. First few: $\Phi_3=c^2+d$, $\Phi_4=c^3+2cd+2dc$.
